title: GPU runbook gaps + experiments — weekly brief
content:
Purpose:
This is the weekly infra brief focused on known runbook gaps for GPU fleet operations, ongoing experiments to reduce tail-latency during regional spikes, and concrete actions for the oncall rotation. Goal is to capture open problems, quick wins, and owners so the SRE oncall and capacity planners have a single working note for this week.

Summary highlights (high level):
- Current global spare capacity estimate: ~6.8% across prod pools (see metric snapshot). Edge regions (ap-southeast-2, eu-west-3) are tighter: 2–3% spare.
- Recent incident (2026-07-30) revealed missing rollback steps for model-variant fallback when a dedicated pool starts preemption.
- Experiment: lightweight prewarm seeding + warm-cache hints reduced 95th token latency by ~18% in the internal test harness.
- Immediate risk: upcoming marketing campaign (expected +45% API QPS for 4 hrs PDT on 2026-08-07) — need temporary capacity plan and autoscale policy check.

Metric snapshot (last 72h, rolling averages):
- Global GPU utilization (prod pools): 71% avg, 95th 94%
- Short window peeks (15m): west-us-2 hit 98% for 12m on 2026-07-30 incident window
- Prefetch/KV cache hit rate: 22% overall (target 30% for steady-state savings)
- Median latency for text-generation (hosted): 190ms; p95 token latency: 1.9s

Runbook gaps discovered (actionable items):
1) Lack of explicit rollback for model-variant downgrade during pool preemption.
   - Problem: when a dedicated pool preempts, there is an automatic fallback to cheaper model-variants but no clear scripted rollback in case of misrouting.
   - Impact: possible higher error rates and customer-visible latency for 3–10 minutes while ops triage.
   - Proposed short fix: add a small stateful checkpoint and a fast parity check (healthprobe) after any automatic fallback.
   - Owner: Jonas Becker. Due: 2026-08-06.

2) Oncall playbook missing section for cross-region warm transfers.
   - Problem: playbook tells how to move capacity but not the validated checklist for KV cache warmup when routing traffic between regions.
   - Impact: first 1000 requests after reroute experience higher tail latency and token-costs due to cold KV caches.
   - Proposed fix: write step-by-step warm-transfer instructions + include a small script to prime top N prefixes.
   - Owner: Rina Matsui. Due: 2026-08-05.

3) No documented pre-surge policy for short marketing bursts (less than 6 hours).
   - Problem: policies assume multi-day commitments and autoscaler configs aren't tuned for <6hr bursts.
   - Impact: either overprovisioning cost blowouts or under-provisioning and rate-limiting.
   - Proposed short-term: implement a temporary buffer pool tied to campaign tags; gating via ops flag.
   - Owner: Marcus Lopez + Product (cc: Elena Ruiz). Due: 2026-08-06.

Ongoing experiments (status and notes):
A) Prewarm seeding + warm-cache hints (internal harness) — iter 3
   - Approach: seed a small set of cached KV prefixes using a synthetic traffic generator that mimics top-200 prompt shards; add an HTTP header hint so runtime prioritizes KV prefetch.
   - Result: p95 token latency reduced 18% in our canary region (testnet), cold start token cost down ~6%.
   - Notes: no customer-facing traffic yet; needs safety test to ensure hints don't alter scheduling fairness.
   - Next: schedule a limited canary for 2 hours in eu-west-1 outside business peak. Owner: Aisha Patel. Planned canary: 2026-08-09 02:00–04:00 UTC.

B) Lightweight batch smoothing for short bursts — PoC
   - Idea: dynamically reduce batching windows by 10–20ms for routes with tight latency SLOs during spikes to allow more concurrent GPU slots and avoid large single-request batches that create jitter.
   - Observed: lower variance but increased token overhead by ~1.3%.
   - Decision point: acceptable tradeoff? Need product input on cost vs latency.
   - Owner: Elena Ruiz. Decision request due: 2026-08-07.

Action items (concrete and prioritized):
- Jonas: Add rollback parity check and operator command for forced revert. (INFRA-742). Due 2026-08-06.
- Rina: Draft cross-region warm-transfer checklist + warm-prime script. Link into oncall playbook. Due 2026-08-05.
- Marcus + Elena: Define campaign buffer pool gating and cost cap. Draft policy for short-lived campaigns. Due 2026-08-06.
- Aisha: Run canary of prewarm seeding in eu-west-1 2026-08-09 and collect p50/p95/p99 baseline. Post results to INFRA-788.
- Oncall (this week): monitor west-us-2 03:00–07:00 PDT daily for any residual preemption pattern tied to vendor reclaim windows.

Open questions / decisions needed from Product and SRE leadership:
- Cost cap threshold for transient campaign buffer pools (proposed $1.2k/hr global cap for 4-hr bursts) — product to confirm acceptability.
- Do we accept 1–2% token overhead to reduce p95 by ~15–20% in latency-critical routes? Product input needed.
- Are we comfortable with KV prefetch hints being included in SDK semantics (privacy/observability implications)? Platform security to weigh in.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: prewarm canary unintentionally prioritizes certain customers during limited rollout. Mitigation: traffic scoped to internal test accounts and synthetic keys; add throttles.
- Risk: warm-prime script may create excess egress or billing anomalies in certain cloud accounts. Mitigation: rate-limit priming and track cost via short-lived budget alerts.

Notes from oncall hand-off (this week):
- Night shift oncall: Priya Singh (contact) — watchlist added for west-us-2 nodes tagged 'dedicated-marketing'.
- Escalation matrix: first pager to eng-infrastructure oncall -> if no ack in 10m -> Core SRE -> Eng manager.
- Quick triage checklist added to Slack ops channel pinned messages.

Appendix: short links to artifacts and test logs
- INFRA-742 (Jira) — rollback parity prototype
- INFRA-788 (Jira) — prewarm seeding canary
- PR: ops-playbooks/pull/129 — initial warm-transfer checklist (WIP)
- Canary logs: s3://internal-ops/logs/prewarm-seed/2026-08-03 (internal)

Bottom line recommendation:
- Ship the three small fixes (rollback parity, warm-transfer checklist, campaign buffer gating) this week as low-risk mitigations.
- Run the prewarm canary in eu-west-1 on 2026-08-09 and reassess whether the prefetch hint approach should be promoted to production.
- Product to confirm cost cap and token-overhead tradeoff by 2026-08-07 so we can finalize the short-burst policy.

-- end of brief --
